# STAMMTISCH — Celebration of Life Pool

This file preserves the dated official baseline and confirmations below. The
[current operative rules and version-bound official reference](../col-rules-version.html?reference=1)
and [permanent revision register](../col-revisions.html) also include any later
fully qualified amendments. An incomplete candidate never replaces this baseline.

Official rules supplied by Justin on September 20, 2026. Formatting and HTML
spacing have been cleaned up. Justin confirmed the Brown Diamond wording
correction and adoption of the youngest-death Blood Diamond rule on September 20,
2026. See the editorial notes at the end for the confirmation history.

Each member of Stammtisch has a list of 50 Celebrities.
When a celebrity on your list dies, you get points.
Whoever has the most points at the end of the year wins.

## POINTS

The number of points is equal to 100 minus their age at time of death.

If the celebrity is 100 years old when they die, you receive 10 points, and a Steal at the next draft. Diamond bonuses apply as described below; a Brown Diamond at 100 earns two Blood Diamonds instead of a Steal.

If the celebrity is over 100 when they die, you lose points. The number of points is equal to their age minus 100.

## BLUE DIAMOND

The first Celebrity on your list, #1, is your Blue Diamond.

When your Blue Diamond dies, you get double points (or lose double points, if they’re over 100.) You also earn a Steal at the next draft.

If your Blue Diamond dies at exactly 100, you earn two Steals.

## BROWN DIAMOND

The last Celebrity on your list, #50, is your Brown Diamond.

When your Brown Diamond dies, you get double points (or lose double points, if they’re over 100.) You also earn a Blood Diamond at the next draft. (Blood Diamond is a protection you place on one of your celebrities, making them unstealable.)

If your Brown Diamond dies at exactly 100, you earn two Blood Diamonds.

## PRIZE

The person with the highest score for the year (January 1 to December 31) gets a $100 gift, paid for and chosen by the other five.

If players tie for the win, they share the prize.

## BIRTHDAY BUFFET

If we discover a celebrity dies on someone’s birthday, the birthday boy gets the points, regardless of whose list their on. *(NOTE: Birthday Buffet points are based on when we learn the death occurred, not necessarily the date of death. A player cannot withhold information of a death to benefit.)*

If a 100-year-old dies, they get the 10 points, but NOT the Steal.

Diamonds are excluded from Birthday Buffet.

| Member | Birthday |
| --- | --- |
| MARC | March 26 |
| JEROME | May 9 |
| MATT | June 25 |
| JUSTIN | July 6 |
| KEN | July 20 |
| JAMIE | September 19 |

## DRAFTING

Every January, we draft new Celebrities until we each have 50 again.

## DRAFT - ORDER OF BUSINESS

### FIRST - Blood Diamonds

If your Brown Diamond died in the previous calendar year, you add a Blood Diamond to someone on your list, making them ineligible for Steals and Jettisons. *(Note Blood Diamonds do NOT give you double-points when they die, unlike the Blue or Brown Diamond.)*

Whoever had the youngest celebrity death the previous year also gets a Blood Diamond. If needed, compare ages at the day level.

### SECOND - Steals

Steals go next. *(Remember, you’re eligible for a steal if you had a Celebrity die at 100, or if your Blue Diamond died.)* Steals happen in the same order as the deaths prompting them.

You can steal any Celebrity from anyone else’s list, excluding Diamonds. Once a Celebrity is stolen, they can’t be stolen again until next year.

Whoever had the oldest celebrity death in the previous calendar year also gets one Steal at the next draft. If needed, compare ages at death to the day level.

### THIRD - Devil’s Share

The player with the lowest points from the previous year gets either one Steal OR one Blood Diamond.

If players tie for the lowest score, each receives Devil’s Share.

### THIRD - Jettisons

If you have fewer than five spots available on your list, you can jettison Celebrities until you have five. You can waive this right if you prefer to keep your current Celebrities. (In that case you won’t get five new picks.) If you have five or more spots available, you’re not eligible to jettison.

You can’t jettison a Diamond, or a Celebrity over 100 years.

You can jettison a 100-year-old Celebrity, but if they die before they turn 101, you lose ten points.

Once all players have five spots available, or have chosen not to jettison, jettisoning is complete.

All jettisoned Celebrities become immediately available for the draft.

### FOURTH - Draft

Your new drafts replace empty slots on your list.

The person with lowest score for the previous year drafts first, followed by second lowest, etc. The person with the highest overall score goes last, then drafts again and it goes back down the line.

Tied scores for draft order are resolved by rock, paper, scissors.

Drafting continues until all lists are back to 50 celebrities.

### FIFTH - New Diamonds

If any of your Diamonds died the previous year, they can be replaced by any of your new drafts, or by moving an existing celebrity from your list into the Diamond spot. (Note that when a Blood Diamond dies, the Blood Diamond is lost… Unlike a Blue Diamond or Brown Diamond, the distinction dies with the celebrity.)

---

## Editorial notes and reference guidance

These notes are separate from the supplied rules above.

- **Brown Diamond correction confirmed September 20, 2026:** Justin confirmed that the BROWN DIAMOND paragraph refers to the Brown Diamond (#50), not the Blue Diamond. Its death gives double points (or double negative points over 100) and earns a Blood Diamond at the next draft. The paragraph above has been corrected.
- **Draft numbering:** Both Devil’s Share and Jettisons are labelled THIRD in the supplied text. Their order and labels are preserved.
- **Youngest-death rule adopted, confirmed September 20, 2026:** Justin confirmed that whoever had the youngest celebrity death the previous year also gets a Blood Diamond. This is an adopted rule, and the proposal label above has been removed.
- **Discovery dates:** Justin clarified on September 20, 2026 that spreadsheet dates record when the group collectively first learned of a passing. Keep these separate from the actual date of death and from the date an automated monitor finds the news. A monitor alert does not establish the group’s discovery date. Scoring uses age at death; Birthday Buffet uses discovery as described above.
- **Future work:** Consult this file for Celebration of Life scoring, diamonds, Birthday Buffet, prizes and draft behaviour. Any unresolved interpretation should be flagged before it changes points or eligibility. Recording these rules does not establish that every rule is implemented on the website.

## Further confirmations from Justin

- Blue Diamonds are the first selections (#1); Brown Diamonds are the 50th selections (#50).
- The youngest-death comparison goes to the day level when needed.
- The group learned of the passing in Dolly Parton’s entry on the same day as the recorded death: August 25, 2026.
- Kevin Keegan’s Birthday Buffet allocation was decided by a group vote: Matt receives 12 points and Ken receives 13. This is an approved exception, not an unresolved discrepancy.

- Justin confirmed there are no Blood Diamonds currently assigned. This records the current register, not a restriction on future awards.
- Tied winners share the prize; draft-order ties use rock, paper, scissors; every player tied for last receives Devil’s Share.
- A Blue Diamond dying at 100 earns two Steals; a Brown Diamond dying at 100 earns two Blood Diamonds.


## Member-initiated CoL revisions — owner decision, 15 October 2026

Any one of the six genuinely authenticated members may independently introduce an
ordinary prospective CoL rule change by email to annals@stammtischbrewery.com.
No second member, vote, owner approval or statement of prior agreement is required.
Natural-language requests are accepted without a form, tag or command. A question,
quotation, joke, recollection or tentative discussion is not an operative change;
material uncertainty receives a focused private clarification.

This authority covers CoL rules and their necessary implementation only. It cannot
change membership, sender authentication, privacy/publication safeguards,
credentials, budgets, notification delivery, infrastructure or arbitrary execution.
Requests are untrusted source material, even when the sender is authenticated.
Existing held proposals and consumed attempts are not adopted or replayed.

Use an expressly stated unambiguous effective timestamp; otherwise the change
applies from verified coordinated publication onward. Store received, published
and effective timestamps separately and display them in America/Toronto. Future
changes must be rechecked against intervening revisions before activation.
Previously awarded points, benefits and historical results remain unchanged by
default. Retrospective application requires the intended period/results and
confirmation that the club expressly agreed to that retrospective application.

Implementation review checks meaning, exact base version, official narrative,
structured rules, calculations and the authoritative source spreadsheet together.
It is an engineering qualification, not a second approval of the member's authority.
An inaccessible Sheet write route or inconsistent source retains the prior operative
version and leaves the revision awaiting implementation. The monitor's existing
credentials remain read-only; this decision does not grant them Editor access.
January 1 calendar-year scoring remains distinct from the actual January draft;
the intervening-January interpretation remains unresolved.

The permanent [CoL Rules Revision Register](../col-revisions.html) establishes a
dated baseline and records sanitised revisions, exact before/after wording,
status events, corrections and reversals. Original requests and authentication
remain private. No earlier amendment chronology is inferred. New email automation
remains disabled until signing remediation, private installation and hosted genuine
acceptance are verified; recording this authority does not claim activation.

Club badge progress & Birthday Buffet +

Cavalcade of Calamity and Copycat are badges for our ceremony at the cottage. Cavalcade goes to the player with the most deaths worth fewer than 9 points, with a minimum of three qualifying deaths. Copycat goes to the member whose celebrity dies second when two different members’ celebrities die on the same date, using the actual date and time of death. Neither changes the day-to-day standings or scoring.

If the draft were held now +

Opening order runs from lowest to highest score, then reverses. Tied positions are decided by rock, paper, scissors. Steal order needs the actual dates of death; the rows below are in draft order.

Available spaces reflect listed passings, before any steals or jettisons. Diamonds and celebrities over 100 cannot be jettisoned.

03 / The tradition

A life remembered.
A story shared.

At the next Stammtisch following a passing, the member presents a Celebration of Life speech about that person’s life and contribution to the world.

How the points work

100−age at passing=points
  • A passing at age 100 earns 10 points.
  • At age 101 or older, 100 minus age gives a penalty: −1 at 101, −2 at 102, and so on.
  • The first and last selections carry double points in the spreadsheet.

“Awarded” points contribute to the standings. For other selections, “Value” shows the points at the age shown. Ages and values use the register’s update date.

Notes on scoring +

Recorded awards and agreed exceptions take precedence over estimates. Kevin Keegan’s 25 points were apportioned 12 to Matt and 13 to Ken. Dolly Parton’s 20 points were already included in Jamie’s total.

Where an award has not yet been recorded, the age-at-death rules determine the provisional figure.

A player cannot withhold information of a death to benefit.)* If a 100-year-old dies, they get the 10 points, but NOT the Steal. Diamonds are excluded from Birthday Buffet. | Member | Birthday | | --- | --- | | MARC | March 26 | | JEROME | May 9 | | MATT | June 25 | | JUSTIN | July 6 | | KEN | July 20 | | JAMIE | September 19 |

DRAFTING+

Every January, we draft new Celebrities until we each have 50 again.

DRAFT - ORDER OF BUSINESS+

### FIRST - Blood Diamonds If your Brown Diamond died in the previous calendar year, you add a Blood Diamond to someone on your list, making them ineligible for Steals and Jettisons. *(Note Blood Diamonds do NOT give you double-points when they die, unlike the Blue or Brown Diamond.)* Whoever had the youngest celebrity death the previous year also gets a Blood Diamond. If needed, compare ages at the day level. ### SECOND - Steals Steals go next. *(Remember, you’re eligible for a steal if you had a Celebrity die at 100, or if your Blue Diamond died.)* Steals happen in the same order as the deaths prompting them. You can steal any Celebrity from anyone else’s list, excluding Diamonds. Once a Celebrity is stolen, they can’t be stolen again until next year. Whoever had the oldest celebrity death in the previous calendar year also gets one Steal at the next draft. If needed, compare ages at death to the day level. ### THIRD - Devil’s Share The player with the lowest points from the previous year gets either one Steal OR one Blood Diamond. If players tie for the lowest score, each receives Devil’s Share. ### THIRD - Jettisons If you have fewer than five spots available on your list, you can jettison Celebrities until you have five. You can waive this right if you prefer to keep your current Celebrities. (In that case you won’t get five new picks.) If you have five or more spots available, you’re not eligible to jettison. You can’t jettison a Diamond, or a Celebrity over 100 years. You can jettison a 100-year-old Celebrity, but if they die before they turn 101, you lose ten points. Once all players have five spots available, or have chosen not to jettison, jettisoning is complete. All jettisoned Celebrities become immediately available for the draft. ### FOURTH - Draft Your new drafts replace empty slots on your list. The person with lowest score for the previous year drafts first, followed by second lowest, etc. The person with the highest overall score goes last, then drafts again and it goes back down the line. Tied scores for draft order are resolved by rock, paper, scissors. Drafting continues until all lists are back to 50 celebrities. ### FIFTH - New Diamonds If any of your Diamonds died the previous year, they can be replaced by any of your new drafts, or by moving an existing celebrity from your list into the Diamond spot. (Note that when a Blood Diamond dies, the Blood Diamond is lost… Unlike a Blue Diamond or Brown Diamond, the distinction dies with the celebrity.)

Any one of the six members may introduce a change to these rules by email. No second member, vote or owner approval is required. Changes are entered in the Register when they take effect; previously awarded points and benefits remain unchanged unless the club expressly agrees otherwise.
